description: Kernel dependency lock for the Android build. The Android app is a shell around scratch-gui, and scratch-gui's own pnpm-lock.yaml decides which scratch-vm / scratch-render build is compiled in. That made the shipped engine a function of whenever CI happened to clone a floating branch, so a build could silently ship a stale kernel. This file is the single source of truth for what is allowed to ship: the exact scratch-gui commit, the engine revisions that commit must resolve to, and the markers that must be present in the compiled bundle. Verified by scripts/verify-engine.mjs. Update with scripts/pin-scratch-gui.mjs after pushing scratch-gui.

scratchGui.why: chore: update pnpm-lock.yaml - the commit that moved the engine pins off 9de42379 (scratch-vm) and f1e1b860 (scratch-render) onto builds that contain the Android renderer OOM fixes. Its parent 6f214ee87 is what origin/develop pointed at while the 2.0.2 APK shipped pre-fix engines.

scratch-vm.why: perf(memory): release orphaned renderer skins when a project is unloaded - releases the outgoing project's skins from Runtime.dispose(), and lowers MAX_CONCURRENT_IMAGE_DECODES from 50 to 12 because the limit is also the peak number of fully decoded bitmaps held at once.

scratch-render.why: perf(memory): cap texture and silhouette size, release orphaned skins - clamps bitmap costumes to maxTextureDimension, samples silhouettes from at most 256 texels, and stops every unselected costume from pinning the decoded bitmap it was built from.

requiredBundleMarkers.why: Runtime.dispose() hands the outgoing project's textures back. Without it, opening project B after A costs A + B, and a single large project never returns its costumes' memory.
BitmapSkin.setBitmap downsizes anything past maxTextureDimension. Without it a 4096x4096 imported costume costs ~64MB of texture plus ~64MB of silhouette, unbounded.
